thm:p15-factorial-two-by-two: H_2 analysis matrix, H_2^T H_2=4I; Delta_A=2beta_A, Delta_B=2beta_B, D_AB=4beta_AB, Delta_A(b)=2beta_A+2(2b-1)beta_AB; zero-one coding gives mu_00, Delta_A(0), Delta_B(0), D_AB

def:p15-factorial-retained-example: retained (4,0,0,2) means give conditional -4 and 2, average -1, D_AB=6; explicit row-space solutions a; missing-cell nonestimability; 'The sign difference in the original four-cell example is retained'

thm:p15-factorial-replication and remark: cell-mean variance sigma^2/n_j, pure-error SS with expectation (N-m)sigma^2, SSE = pure error + lack of fit; repeated measurements on one unit have variance sigma_U^2+sigma_e^2/q; the participant remains the assigned unit

completely randomized and blocked designs (NIST 5.3.3.1-5.3.3.2 examples) and thm:p15-factorial-blocks: treatment contrast eliminates every additive block effect, variance sigma^2 sum c_t^2/B, residual df (L-1)(B-1) cannot separate interaction from pure error

thm:p15-factorial-centers-blocks: block column equals chi_123 on the corners (only the sum is identified); within-block replication keeps its own assignment unit
annex:p15.factorial.replication and annex:p15.factorial.blocks: written proofs

def/thm:p15-w02b-p15-075-blocked: blocked variance depends only on within-block spread ('That is the gain from blocking'); one unit per treatment per block gives no design-based variance estimate; repeated measurements remain one assigned unit
annex:p15-w02b-p15-075-blocked: written proof
thm:p15-w02b-p15-076-families: replication divides ||a_*||^2 by n with nu_n=nN_1-r; complete blocks; cluster assignment design effect 1+(m-1)rho versus individual assignment

Replacing (beta_3, beta_12) by (beta_3+t, beta_12-t) leaves every fitted response unchanged. Only their sum is recovered.'; complete alias classes I=123, 1=23, 2=13, 3=12 and the negative fraction

annex:p15.factorial.estimability: written proof of indistinguishability

def:p15-factorial-assignment and thm:p15-factorial-assignment: the warranted target is the assignment contrast tau for the recruited units, unbiasedly estimated under known positive assignment probabilities; P19 weights (0,0,-1,1) and (-1,1,-1,1)/2 (the estimable a-vectors of lines 107-110); noncompliance, missingness, interference and generalization limits

thm:p15-factorial-mechanism and remark: complete estimation of the factorial surface does not identify the mechanism; the additional premise is stated as process measurements with an explicit measurement model, interventions or controls that separate competing mechanisms, and assumptions connecting them to the causal equations; estimability, uncertainty, assignment effect and mechanism each have their own premises
annex:p15.factorial.assignment and annex:p15.factorial.mechanism: written proofs (two structural models with the same assignment surface and different responses to intervening on R)
thm:p15-w02b-p15-075-licenses: what random assignment licenses (unbiased estimator of tau for recruited units) versus random sampling without assignment
what the results do not license: assignment estimate concerns tau only; a mechanism claim needs further premises (thm:p15-factorial-mechanism)
def:p15-w02b-p15-077-study-premises: premises under which the target is the assignment contrast; a mechanism claim needs the additional evidence stated after thm:p15-factorial-mechanism
def:p15-w02b-p15-077-limits: identification does not deliver a statement about the process through which assignment acts

defect_observations.observation: For the source's alternative 2^(8-3) design (6=12345, 7=135, 8=245) the handbook states that exactly 12, 14, 23, 34 are clear and twenty-four two-factor interactions are aliased (annex 333-337: 27=46 from I=2467). The held source (E-Handbook.pdf PDF p. 1345, section 5.3.3.4.4) says 23 of 28 are confounded and lists 27 among the estimable interactions. The handbook's count follows from the defining relation it states, but the text presents the design as the source's without recording that it departs from the source's own statement.

The five-level Hyper-Graeco-Latin matrix has E13 in row 3, column 4. That agrees with the source's full design table (PDF p. 1318, run 3 4 1 3 5), but the source's compact display (PDF p. 1319) prints E31. The claim at 292-298 that the compact matrices retain all runs holds against the full design table, but the inconsistency inside the source is not recorded.

The chapter roadmap says the final section 'states the additional conditions under which an estimable contrast is an effect of assignment or an identified causal mechanism'. Lines 728-741 prove non-identification and list the kinds of additional evidence and assumptions, but they give no conditions under which the mechanism is identified. C04 still holds, because it asks only for the additional premise, but the roadmap claims more than the section delivers.
